hero.headline: House GOP seeks end to floor standoff with conservative faction
hero.body:
House Republican leaders are working to resolve a weeks-long standoff with conservative members that has brought legislative activity to a halt. The dispute centers on demands from hard-line Republicans that party leaders take stronger action on the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act, known as the SAVE America bill.

The floor paralysis has prevented the House from conducting regular business for two weeks. Conservative members have used procedural tactics to block votes and other chamber activities until their demands are met. House GOP leaders are hoping to make progress on resolving the impasse, though the path forward remains uncertain.

The SAVE America Act relates to voter eligibility requirements, though conservative members have pressed for more aggressive moves on the legislation than leadership has been willing to pursue. The standoff represents a familiar challenge for House Speaker Mike Johnson, who like his predecessors has faced pressure from the party's most conservative wing to take harder-line positions on policy priorities.

The disruption comes as House Republicans hold a narrow majority, giving small groups of members significant leverage to influence the legislative agenda. Similar standoffs have occurred repeatedly in recent years, with conservative factions using procedural tools to extract concessions from leadership. The current impasse has prevented consideration of other legislation and routine chamber business.

Leadership hopes to see movement toward a resolution that would allow the House to resume normal operations. The duration of previous standoffs has varied, with some resolved within days and others stretching longer as negotiations continue between leadership and the demanding members.

cards.headline: US and Iran exchange attacks for third day as conflict over Strait of Hormuz intensifies
cards.body:
The United States and Iran continued their military escalation for a third consecutive night, with American forces conducting fresh strikes on Iranian targets while Tehran responded with attacks on commercial shipping and a military facility.

US Central Command said it shot down four Iranian attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz and struck a ground control station in Iran's Bandar Abbas that was preparing to launch a fifth drone. Officials characterized the actions as "measured, purely defensive, and intended to maintain the ceasefire." Approximately two hours later, Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed they had targeted an American military base in Kuwait in retaliation, with Kuwait's military confirming it intercepted hostile missile and drone threats around 6am local time.

The tit-for-tat strikes occurred as Iranian forces also fired at four vessels attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran's state broadcaster IRIB, which reported the incident happened around 12:35am local time without providing further details about the ships.

The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical chokepoint for global energy markets, with roughly a fifth of the world's petroleum passing through this passage between Iran and the Arabian Peninsula. The waterway connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and the wider Indian Ocean.

President Trump announced a significant policy shift, declaring that the United States would reinstate a maritime blockade on Iran and impose a 20 percent charge on cargo transiting the strait. This represents a departure from long-standing US policy supporting free navigation through international waterways. The UAE condemned Iran's attack on two national tankers in the southern lane of the strait in Omani territorial waters, which killed one Indian crew member and wounded eight others.

The escalation comes amid stalled negotiations between Washington and Tehran. Trump stated that Iran wants "very much to make a deal" but that the US was "not satisfied" with current proposals. He warned that if negotiations failed, "we'll have to just finish the job," while claiming Iran was "negotiating on fumes."

Trump also appeared to direct an unusual warning at Oman, a US ally, over reports that Iran and Oman might jointly manage the strait. He said the waterway would be "open to everybody" and suggested Oman would need to comply with US requirements or face military action.

A key sticking point in negotiations remains whether any US-Iran ceasefire will cover Israel's military operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon. Iran has insisted that Lebanon must be included in any ceasefire agreement. Israel has intensified its operations in Lebanon, with the military striking 550 targets since the beginning of the week and pushing forces farther north against Hezbollah fighters. More than 1.2 million Lebanese have been displaced since fighting escalated in March.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Climb Above $85 Per Barrel as Tensions Rise in Persian Gulf
cards.body:
Brent crude oil breached $85 per barrel on Monday, reaching its highest price in a month as escalating military confrontations between the United States and Iran intensified concerns about energy supplies. The price jump reflected trader concerns about disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway that handles roughly 20 million barrels of oil daily under normal conditions.

The recent spike came after fresh U.S. strikes on Iranian targets, including missile launch sites and mine-laying vessels. These attacks dashed hopes that a diplomatic breakthrough might ease the standoff and allow exports to resume through the blocked strait. The conflict has already cut 14.4 million barrels of oil per day from the Gulf's prewar output, creating significant supply pressures in global energy markets.

The Trump administration's proposal to impose a 20 percent toll on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz to cover "safety and security" costs added another layer of uncertainty to market conditions. This announcement pushed traders to reassess risks to oil flows and their implications for global supplies.

U.S. crude also climbed above $80 per barrel as markets absorbed the latest developments. Energy analysts noted that weeks of disruption have heavily depleted global crude stockpiles and fuel reserves. Emergency releases from strategic reserves have provided only limited relief, offsetting about 2 million barrels daily of the 14.4 million barrel shortfall. These emergency draws are expected to end by July, with inventories already critically low according to investment analysts.

The International Energy Agency warned that the world could reach a critical point in July and August, when demand for summer travel fuels will surge while production capacity remains constrained. This mismatch between supply and demand could force additional emergency measures and further price volatility.

The price escalation has immediate consequences for consumers. In the United Kingdom, petrol prices reached their highest levels since the conflict began, with the average price now 159.43 pence per liter, an increase of 26.6 pence since late February. Energy bills are expected to rise sharply as well, with typical household heating costs forecast to increase by nearly 13 percent.

Airlines are already responding to higher fuel costs. Delta Airlines reported record fuel expenses but said it has passed along 60 percent of additional costs to consumers through higher ticket prices. The company indicated it plans to eventually pass along all elevated fuel costs to passengers.

Market observers remain cautious about prospects for relief. While traders periodically respond to reports of potential peace agreements, each diplomatic optimism has been followed by renewed escalation. As one analyst noted, the pattern resembles "an endless loop" of hopes repeatedly dashed by new military developments. Even in a best-case scenario where flows through the Strait of Hormuz normalize, markets are expected to remain tight given critically low inventory levels.

cards.headline: U.S. to begin blockade of Iranian ships in Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: The U.S. military will start blocking Iranian vessels in the strategic waterway as Iran vows to maintain its own control.
cards.body:
The U.S. military announced plans to reinstate a blockade of Iranian ships in the Strait of Hormuz beginning Tuesday. Iran responded by asserting its intention to control the strategic waterway, escalating tensions in the region.

The move threatens to destabilize the critical international shipping channel after the two countries had recently agreed to a ceasefire. The dispute raises concerns about potential disruptions to global energy markets and maritime trade through one of the world's most vital oil and commercial shipping passages.

cards.headline: Yemen's Houthis fire missiles at Saudi airport after Sanaa strike
cards.teaser: The Iran-backed group blamed Saudi Arabia for an attack on Yemen's capital and launched missiles at Abha airport in response.
cards.body:
The Iran-backed Houthi movement launched a missile attack on Abha airport in southwestern Saudi Arabia. The group said the strike was in response to attacks on Sanaa airport in Yemen's capital, which they attributed to Saudi forces.

This escalation marks another chapter in the ongoing conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis. Saudi Arabia has led a military coalition in Yemen's civil war since 2015, while the Houthis control much of northern Yemen, including the capital.

cards.headline: European Union bans gold imports from Sudan to cut war funding
cards.teaser: The ban also restricts exports of mercury and cyanide to Sudan, chemicals used in gold mining operations.
cards.body:
The European Union has banned gold imports from Sudan as part of efforts to restrict funding for the country's civil war. The measure also prohibits EU exports of mercury and cyanide to Sudan, chemicals essential to gold mining operations.

Gold production has become a major revenue source for armed groups operating in Sudan, particularly in areas outside government control. By cutting off these economic channels, the EU aims to weaken the financial foundations sustaining the ongoing conflict.

cards.headline: Congress considers quick passage of Russia sanctions bill as Graham tribute
cards.teaser: Lawmakers are pushing to advance bipartisan Russia sanctions legislation authored by the late Sen. Lindsey Graham as a way to honor him.
cards.body:
Supporters of Ukraine in Congress are urging swift passage of bipartisan Russia sanctions legislation that Graham had authored. Graham announced a breakthrough on the bill shortly before his death, saying lawmakers had reached agreement with the White House on the measure.

The push to move the legislation quickly represents an effort by colleagues to honor Graham's work on the issue. The bill addresses sanctions related to Russia, though the specific provisions were not detailed. Graham's announcement of the deal came late last week before his death on Saturday night.

cards.headline: China expels senior Politburo member over corruption and sexual misconduct
cards.teaser: Ma Xingrui becomes the third Politburo member purged since 2022 in an ongoing anti-graft campaign.
cards.body:
China expelled Ma Xingrui from the Communist Party following an investigation into corruption and sexual misconduct charges. Ma previously served as the top official in Xinjiang and headed China's space program before joining the Politburo, one of the party's most powerful bodies.

The expulsion marks the third time since 2022 that a Politburo member has been purged as part of President Xi Jinping's anti-corruption drive. Investigators said Ma's violations included rampant corruption that extended to family members, though specific details about the charges were not provided in official statements.

cards.headline: European Union bans gold imports from Sudan to cut war funding
cards.teaser: The ban also restricts exports of mercury and cyanide to Sudan, chemicals used in gold mining operations.

cards.headline: Fire near Paris forces evacuations as 10 remain missing in Spain
cards.teaser: A major wildfire in the historic Fontainebleau forest triggered evacuations, while Spanish authorities continue searching for missing persons.
cards.body:
A large fire broke out in the Fontainebleau forest southeast of Paris, prompting authorities to evacuate nearby areas. Firefighting planes were deployed from southern France to combat the blaze threatening the historic woodland, which has served as a popular recreation area and royal hunting ground for centuries.

In Spain, rescue teams continued searching for 10 people still missing from a separate wildfire. The parallel blazes highlight the severe fire conditions affecting parts of Europe during the summer season.

cards.headline: Bangkok bar fire death toll reaches 30 as investigation focuses on locked exits
cards.teaser: Survivors and first responders reported locked doors and missing emergency exit signage at the music venue.
cards.body:
A fire at a Bangkok music bar killed 30 people, making it the city's deadliest blaze in 17 years. An initial assessment found an electrical short circuit in an air conditioner in the ceiling sparked the fire early Monday morning.

Investigators are examining whether negligence contributed to the high death toll. Survivors and emergency responders reported locked doors and unclear emergency exit signage. Many victims were found trapped in windowless bathrooms where they had sought refuge. More than 70 people were injured, with 24 in critical condition. The bar owner said it would cooperate with the investigation.

cards.headline: Passenger nearly sucked out of Ryanair plane during flight
cards.teaser: The man's wife told Serbian media her husband is seriously injured and in shock after the incident.
cards.body:
A passenger on a Ryanair flight experienced a terrifying incident when he was nearly pulled out of the aircraft during what appears to have been a sudden decompression event. His wife, Svetlana Grković, held onto his legs for around five minutes to prevent him from being sucked out of the window.

Grković told Serbian media that her husband suffered serious injuries and remains in shock following the ordeal. She described facing the frightening prospect of dying together during the emergency.

hero.headline: National Guard deployment in Washington extended through 2029
hero.body:
President Trump has extended the deployment of National Guard troops in Washington, D.C., with the mission now set to continue until Inauguration Day 2029. The extension represents the latest in a series of prolongations of the military presence in the nation's capital.

As of recent reports, nearly 2,400 National Guard troops are stationed in Washington, D.C. The ongoing deployment costs approximately $1 million daily. Pete Hegseth, who leads the U.S. Department of Defense, authorized the most recent extension, which pushed the end date from November through at least February and ultimately to January 20, 2029.

The National Guard's extended presence in the capital has drawn legal challenges. Washington D.C. Attorney General Brian Schwalb sued the Trump administration over the deployments, describing them as an "involuntary military occupation" and an illegal use of the military for domestic law enforcement. A federal judge in California previously ruled that Trump's deployment of National Guard troops to Los Angeles following protests had been illegal, though that ruling does not directly apply to Washington, where the president has greater authority over Guard operations than in states.

This deployment marks part of a broader federal strategy to address crime and civil unrest. Following the initial Washington deployment, Trump has sent National Guard troops to Chicago and threatened deployments to Democratic-led cities including San Francisco, Portland and New York. These actions represent a significant escalation in federal intervention into local policing and have prompted strong objections from Democratic officials and community organizers.

The Pentagon has taken additional steps to expand National Guard capabilities for domestic operations. In October, a top military official ordered National Guard units across all 50 states, the District of Columbia, and U.S. territories to establish "quick reaction forces" trained in riot control tactics. The forces are being trained to use batons, body shields, Tasers and pepper spray according to an internal Pentagon directive. The directive set training thresholds for each state, requiring most states to train 500 National Guard members, totaling approximately 23,500 troops nationwide. States are required to report monthly on their progress.

The extended timeline means Guard personnel will remain stationed in Washington for multiple years beyond the current date. National Guard deployments typically require authorization from the president or state governors, with federal activations allowing Guard members to operate under federal command and funding. Service members deployed under federal orders serve on active duty status and receive federal pay and benefits.

The 2029 end date aligns with the conclusion of the current presidential term, suggesting the deployment is tied to the administration's broader security strategy for the capital region. National Guard units traditionally support civilian authorities during emergencies and natural disasters, though extended peacetime deployments in the capital represent a departure from conventional Guard missions.

cards.headline: Supreme Court justices to testify before Congress on security funding
cards.teaser: Justices Barrett and Kagan will make a rare appearance on Capitol Hill to request additional security resources.
cards.body:
Supreme Court justices will make a rare appearance before Congress to request additional funding for security measures. Justices Amy Coney Barrett and Elena Kagan are scheduled to testify on behalf of the Court.

The request comes during a period of increased threats and tensions directed at the judiciary. The justices will seek congressional approval for expanded protective resources to enhance security for Court members and facilities.

cards.headline: Federal agents kill man in Maine
cards.teaser: A man was killed by federal agents in Maine in an incident that remains under investigation.
cards.body:
U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) fatally shot a 26-year-old Colombian man during an immigration operation in Maine. The incident occurred recently as part of enforcement activity by the federal agency.

The shooting comes less than a week after an undocumented migrant was killed by an immigration agent in Houston, highlighting a pattern of lethal force during immigration operations.

cards.headline: States file lawsuit to block Paramount-Warner Bros merger
cards.teaser: Multiple states are taking legal action to prevent the merger of two major entertainment companies.
cards.body:
Several states have filed a lawsuit to block the $110 billion merger between Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros Discovery. A bipartisan coalition of state attorneys general, led by California's Rob Bonta, argues the combination would reduce competition and result in higher consumer prices and thousands of job losses.

Bonta has been a vocal opponent of the merger since it was announced in February following a competitive bidding process that also involved Netflix.

cards.headline: AI technology expands into children's toys and robots
cards.teaser: Artificial intelligence is moving beyond chatbots into playthings designed to interact with children.
cards.body:
AI technology is increasingly being incorporated into toys, dolls, and robots built to befriend children. A child-development expert says the technology offers potential benefits but also carries risks of displacing human relationships that children need for healthy development.

The expansion of AI into childhood products marks a shift from screen-based interactions to physical toys with conversational capabilities. The technology raises questions about how AI companions might affect child development, social skills, and family dynamics as these products become more sophisticated and widespread in homes.

cards.headline: Counter-terrorism police take over Ann Widdecombe murder investigation
cards.teaser: A 28-year-old suspect was re-arrested after counter-terrorism officers assumed control of the case.
cards.body:
Police continue to question a suspect in the murder of Ann Widdecombe after counter-terrorism police took over the investigation. The 28-year-old white British male suspect was re-arrested on Monday following the transfer of the case to counter-terrorism authorities.

The shift to counter-terrorism investigators suggests potential concerns about the motivation or circumstances of the killing. Counter-terrorism police handle cases that may involve extremist ideology or threats to public safety beyond conventional criminal investigations.

cards.headline: JPMorgan and Wells Fargo Report Quarterly Earnings
cards.teaser: Major U.S. banks released their latest financial results, kicking off earnings season for the financial sector.
cards.body:
JPMorgan and Wells Fargo disclosed their quarterly earnings, providing insight into the health of large American financial institutions. Wall Street banks are expected to report strong trading revenues for the quarter, with projections approaching $39 billion across the sector.

The earnings releases come as investors seek clarity on how banks are performing amid economic uncertainty. Analysts are examining whether the results will ease concerns about the broader economic outlook. The reports also coincide with a return of dealmaking activity, which has contributed to improved performance at investment banking divisions.

cards.headline: California Leads 12-State Lawsuit Against Paramount Warner Bros Merger
cards.teaser: California and 11 other states filed a lawsuit seeking to block the proposed merger of the two major entertainment studios.
cards.body:
California has joined 11 other states in a bipartisan lawsuit seeking to block the $110 billion merger between Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery. California Attorney General Rob Bonta is leading the coalition, having opposed the deal since it was announced in February following a competitive bidding process.

The state attorneys general argue the merger would reduce competition in the entertainment industry, leading to higher consumer prices and thousands of job losses. Both studios maintain headquarters in California, making the state a key jurisdiction in the legal challenge to the proposed combination.

cards.headline: U.S. Worker Productivity Reaches New Highs Without AI
cards.teaser: American workers are producing more output per hour than ever before, driven by factors predating widespread artificial intelligence adoption.
cards.body:
Companies have been extracting increased productivity from employees over several years through factors unrelated to AI technology. Tight labor markets have pushed workers and employers to find efficiencies, while digitization and remote work arrangements have contributed to output gains.

These productivity improvements demonstrate that businesses have found ways to boost performance through operational changes and workforce management strategies. The trend has implications for wage growth, corporate profitability, and economic growth potential.

cards.headline: Apple Accuses Former Employee of Downloading Confidential Files Before Joining OpenAI
cards.teaser: Apple claims a former worker exploited a software vulnerability to access and download proprietary information before departing for the AI company.
cards.body:
Apple has filed legal action against a former employee who allegedly exploited a security vulnerability to download confidential files from the company's network after joining OpenAI. According to Apple, the employee accessed sensitive information well after departing the company, using what the tech giant described as a "rare" bug in its systems.

The lawsuit underscores growing tensions between Apple and OpenAI as both companies compete in artificial intelligence development. The case raises questions about intellectual property protection when employees transition between rival technology firms working on comparable products.

cards.headline: California Introduces Instant Rebates for Electric Vehicle Purchases
cards.teaser: Governor Newsom signed legislation providing point-of-sale discounts for EV buyers, including incentives for used vehicles.
cards.body:
California will offer $3,500 rebates to first-time buyers of certain new electric vehicles, with the incentives applied directly at purchase rather than requiring customers to wait for reimbursement. The program also includes $1,750 discounts for used EVs priced under $25,000.

Governor Newsom framed the initiative as maintaining California's leadership in clean vehicle adoption amid shifting federal policies. The instant rebate structure aims to make the financial benefit more immediate and accessible to consumers considering electric vehicles.

cards.headline: China Removes Top Official on Corruption and Sex Charges
cards.teaser: Ma Xingrui becomes the third Politburo member purged since 2022, following allegations of misconduct.
cards.body:
Chinese authorities have expelled Ma Xingrui from senior leadership positions based on corruption and sex-related charges. Ma previously led the Xinjiang region and served as head of China's space program before his elevation to the Politburo.

The removal marks the third such purge of a Politburo member in recent years, reflecting ongoing anti-corruption efforts within China's top political ranks. The action removes a figure who held significant authority over both regional governance and national space initiatives.

hero.headline: SpaceX prepares Starship for 13th test flight with new satellite tests
hero.body:
SpaceX is gearing up for Starship's 13th test flight later this week, according to company announcements. The upcoming mission will push the spacecraft under higher pressure conditions than previous flights and include tests of new Starlink satellites in orbit.

The test represents the next phase in SpaceX's development of Starship, its next-generation heavy-lift launch system. The vehicle combines a massive Super Heavy booster with the Starship upper stage, designed eventually to carry cargo and crew to orbit and beyond. Previous test flights have progressively demonstrated key capabilities including landing procedures and thermal protection performance.

SpaceX engineers have modified flight parameters for this mission to test Starship under increased stress compared to earlier flights. The company aims to gather data on how the spacecraft performs under more demanding conditions, information that will support future design improvements and refinements to the vehicle's structure and thermal systems.

Beyond the vehicle stress tests, the mission will carry a payload of new Starlink satellites into orbit. These satellites represent an updated design for SpaceX's internet constellation, which currently comprises thousands of satellites in low Earth orbit. The flight will validate whether the satellites can be successfully deployed from Starship and function properly once operational. This test advances SpaceX's goal of using Starship as a launch platform for future Starlink deployments, potentially allowing the company to place many more satellites per launch than its existing Falcon 9 rocket can carry.

The launch timing later this week depends on final vehicle preparations and regulatory approvals from the Federal Aviation Administration. SpaceX has conducted twelve previous Starship test flights, each building on lessons learned from earlier attempts. The program has progressed significantly from early prototype tests that ended in explosions to more recent flights that have achieved controlled returns and ocean landings.

This incremental development approach reflects SpaceX's strategy for creating a fully reusable launch system. The company has described its methodology as a "fly, fail, fix" approach to rocket development, which often involves spectacular failures that provide valuable data for improvement.

SpaceX was recently cleared to resume Starship test flights after a booster failure in May. This 13th flight marks the first Starship test since SpaceX became a public company, testing the market's appetite for the company's developmental approach. The mission will continue the pattern of pushing the vehicle's capabilities while gathering critical engineering data to support SpaceX's long-term goals for the Starship program.

cards.headline: Amazon listings leak Google Pixel 11 pricing and specifications
cards.teaser: Deleted Amazon product pages revealed pricing and full specifications for Google's upcoming Pixel 11 smartphone lineup before the official launch.
cards.body:
Amazon briefly posted product listings for Google's unreleased Pixel 11 series before removing them. The deleted pages revealed pricing information and detailed specifications for multiple models in the lineup across nine color options. The listings appeared to show three different models in the Pixel 11 family.

The leaked information included specifications for the Tensor G6 processor that will power the devices. The listings provided details on the phones' features and configurations well ahead of Google's planned announcement. The premature posting marks another instance of retail listings exposing product details before manufacturers intend to reveal them.

cards.headline: Pinwheel releases landline phone designed for children
cards.teaser: A kid-friendly tech company introduced a landline phone that allows children to stay connected without smartphone features.
cards.body:
Kid-friendly tech company Pinwheel has announced a new landline phone for children. The retro-inspired device allows kids to stay connected without the distractions present in smartphones.

The product is positioned as an alternative for families looking to reduce children's screen time and limit access to smartphone applications and internet features.

cards.headline: SpaceX launches 27 Starlink satellites from California
cards.teaser: A Falcon 9 rocket carried 27 Starlink internet satellites into orbit from Vandenberg Space Force Base in a morning launch.
cards.body:
SpaceX successfully launched 27 Starlink satellites aboard a Falcon 9 rocket from Vandenberg Space Force Base. The mission took place early in the morning and deployed the satellites to join the company's expanding internet constellation. The launch marked another addition to the thousands of Starlink satellites already in orbit.

The Falcon 9 first stage booster used in the mission was flight-proven, having flown previous missions. SpaceX continues its regular cadence of Starlink launches to build out global internet coverage. The company operates the largest commercial satellite constellation, providing internet service to customers in dozens of countries.

cards.headline: Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 specifications surface in leak
cards.teaser: A new leak reportedly exposed nearly complete technical specifications for Samsung's upcoming Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 smartwatch.
cards.body:
Technical specifications for Samsung's unreleased Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 have leaked online. The information reportedly includes detailed hardware specifications for the upcoming smartwatch model. Samsung has separately announced plans for artificial intelligence-powered health features in future wearable devices.

Additional leaks have revealed pricing information and Bluetooth version details for both the Galaxy Watch 9 and Watch Ultra 2 models. The leaked specifications suggest what hardware improvements Samsung plans to include in the new devices. The company has not yet officially announced release dates or confirmed the leaked specifications.

cards.headline: Uber executive discusses expansion into hotels and autonomous vehicles
cards.teaser: Uber's Chief Product Officer outlined the company's plans for financial services, robotaxi partnerships, and artificial intelligence features.
cards.body:
Uber Chief Product Officer Sachin Kansal outlined the company's expansion into new business areas, including financial services and autonomous vehicles. He discussed Uber's relationship with self-driving technology company Waymo and detailed the company's new AV Labs data operation dedicated to advancing self-driving capabilities.

Kansal emphasized that Uber is strategically selective about expansion, rejecting a "everything for everyone" approach. He highlighted how artificial intelligence is being integrated into features that riders and drivers will directly experience, while the company balances partnerships with vehicle manufacturers as it develops its robotaxi ambitions.

cards.headline: Tech entrepreneurs return to startups despite prior success
cards.teaser: Previously successful technology founders are launching new companies focused on artificial intelligence opportunities.
cards.body:
A wave of successful technology entrepreneurs are launching new companies, with many focusing on artificial intelligence applications. These repeat founders view the current moment as a defining opportunity in the tech sector and are drawn back to the demanding work of building startups despite having already created profitable businesses.

The trend reflects concerns among established tech leaders about missing critical developments in artificial intelligence. The potential for significant financial returns from AI ventures appears to motivate founders who might otherwise retire or pursue passive investment strategies. Industry observers note that repeat founders are concentrating their efforts on AI rather than other technology sectors.

hero.headline: Brighton sign Croatia defender Vuskovic from Tottenham for club record £46 million
hero.body:
Brighton have completed the signing of Croatia defender Luka Vuskovic from Tottenham Hotspur for a club record fee of £46 million, with an additional £4 million available through easily achievable add-ons. The 19-year-old has agreed a five-year contract with the option of a further year.

Vuskovic becomes Brighton's most expensive signing, surpassing their previous transfer record. Tottenham retain matching rights should Brighton agree to sell the player in future, plus a 20 percent sell-on clause if he moves to another club.

The centre-back joined Tottenham last summer from Croatian club Hajduk Split for £10 million but never featured for the north London side. He spent the previous season on loan at Hamburg to gain playing experience before this permanent move to Brighton.

Despite his youth, Vuskovic has already earned recognition at international level. The defender became Croatia's youngest World Cup player when he started against England, demonstrating his readiness for top-level football despite his age.

Brighton have built a reputation for acquiring young talent and developing players before selling them on at significant profit. Vuskovic fits this established model, arriving as a prospect with international experience and considerable room for development. His signing reflects Brighton's continued strategy of investing in promising young players who can grow within their system.

The substantial fee paid by Brighton signals the club's confidence in the player's potential and their ambition in the transfer market. The club option for an additional year provides flexibility for both parties as Vuskovic settles into his new environment and competes for a starting position in Brighton's defence.

Vuskovic's transfer comes as part of significant activity in the transfer market involving several Premier League clubs. Tottenham, managed by Roberto De Zerbi, have been particularly active in rebuilding their squad following a disappointing 17th place finish last season. Beyond the Vuskovic sale, Spurs have strengthened their squad through multiple signings as they look to improve on their previous campaign.

Brighton's pursuit of Vuskovic demonstrates their continued investment in defensive reinforcements. The five-year commitment with the additional option shows the club's long-term planning and belief that the Croatian centre-back can develop into a key player for their future.

The signing represents Brighton's latest addition to their squad as they prepare for the upcoming season. Vuskovic will have the opportunity to establish himself as a regular starter in the Premier League following his loan spell abroad, providing him with consistent first-team football at the highest level of English football.

cards.headline: Jordan Walker wins Home Run Derby with late surge against Kyle Schwarber
cards.teaser: Walker homered on his final six swings to defeat Schwarber in the Home Run Derby final.
cards.body:
Jordan Walker staged a comeback in the Home Run Derby, hitting home runs on his last six swings to defeat Kyle Schwarber in the final. The rally allowed Walker to overcome Schwarber, who was competing in front of his home crowd at Citizens Bank Park in Philadelphia.

Walker's late surge silenced the Philadelphia crowd that had been supporting Schwarber throughout the competition. The victory marked a successful Derby appearance for Walker, who demonstrated power and timing when it mattered most in the final round.

cards.headline: White Sox sign top draft pick Roch Cholowsky to record $10.35 million deal
cards.teaser: The first overall pick in the 2026 MLB Draft signed the largest deal for a number one selection.
cards.body:
The Chicago White Sox signed first overall pick Roch Cholowsky to a $10.35 million contract, setting a new record for the largest signing bonus for a number one draft pick. The deal was finalized following the 2026 MLB Draft.

Cholowsky was selected first overall by the White Sox in this year's draft. The record-breaking contract reflects the organization's commitment to securing their top selection and his perceived value as a prospect entering professional baseball.

cards.headline: France faces Spain in World Cup semifinal featuring Mbappe and Yamal
cards.teaser: The semifinal matchup pits two unbeaten teams against each other with star players on both sides.
cards.body:
France and Spain clash in a World Cup semifinal on Tuesday, with both teams seeking revenge and redemption. France midfielder Zaïre-Emery said Les Bleus want to exact revenge on Spain after their painful exit in the Euro 2024 semifinal. Spain won that encounter in Munich two years ago, but France have since revitalized their fortunes with scintillating attacking football to reach this stage.

The match will feature a showdown between Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal, two of the tournament's standout players. The winner advances to the World Cup final, with the stakes higher than any previous encounter between these rivals.

cards.headline: England to face Argentina in World Cup semifinal with increased security in Atlanta
cards.teaser: Authorities announced enhanced security measures for Wednesday's semifinal match.
cards.body:
Atlanta police have stepped up security measures ahead of Wednesday's World Cup semifinal between England and Argentina. The department is deploying additional officers around the stadium and across entertainment and high-traffic areas throughout the city.

The enhanced security response reflects expectations of large crowds before and after the match. Police have increased staffing and resources citywide as Atlanta prepares to host the high-profile fixture and accommodate the influx of residents and visitors.

cards.headline: The Open Championship begins at Royal Birkdale
cards.teaser: Golfers compete at Royal Birkdale in the 2026 British Open with multiple contenders in the field.
cards.body:
The Open Championship is underway at Royal Birkdale, with golfers competing for the Claret Jug. The tournament continues through the week at the historic links course.

English golfers are seeking to end a drought dating back nearly 60 years to Tony Jacklin's 1967 victory, the last time an Englishman won The Open on English soil. There is potential for that streak to be broken this week.

cards.headline: Marion Bartoli discusses friendship with France coach Didier Deschamps
cards.teaser: Former Wimbledon champion spoke about her relationship with the France manager.
cards.body:
Marion Bartoli, the 2013 Wimbledon champion, has spoken about her friendship with France national team coach Didier Deschamps. She describes him as both a winner and a true friend, offering a personal perspective on the man leading France's World Cup campaign.

Deschamps is currently steering France through the tournament, with the team preparing for a heavyweight semi-final clash against Spain in Dallas. The France boss has predicted the encounter will be a "spectacular" match between two exciting sides.

hero.headline: California and 11 Other States Sue to Block Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger
hero.body:
California's attorney general has spearheaded a coalition of 12 state attorneys general in filing a lawsuit to block the $110 billion merger between Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery. The bipartisan group argues that the deal would reduce competition and harm consumers through higher prices.

Rob Bonta, California's attorney general, has been a vocal critic of the merger since it was announced in February following a competitive bidding process that included Netflix. California's leading role in the legal challenge reflects the state's significant stake in the outcome, given that both studios maintain headquarters there.

The states contend that combining these two major entertainment companies would hurt competition across multiple sectors of the industry. The lawsuit warns that the consolidation could result in thousands of job losses while diminishing consumer choice in film distribution, television production, and streaming services. Attorneys general typically pursue antitrust actions when they believe a merger threatens fair competition or market conditions.

The combined entity would control substantial intellectual property portfolios, including classic films, television networks, and streaming platforms. Both Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery operate extensive production facilities, distribution networks, and content libraries that overlap significantly across entertainment sectors.

The legal challenge comes amid continued consolidation in the media industry as companies adapt to shifting distribution models and the growth of streaming services. Traditional studios have pursued mergers to compete more effectively with technology companies that have entered content production. However, regulators at both state and federal levels have increased their scrutiny of major media mergers in recent years.

The merger has already faced some regulatory approval. Trump's Department of Justice approved the deal on Friday, though international regulatory hurdles remain. The approval from federal authorities does not prevent state-level challenges to the transaction.

The lawsuit raises questions about whether the merger would reduce competition sufficient to harm consumers or competitors. Demonstrating this impact will be central to the states' case against the deal. The outcome could significantly reshape the entertainment industry's structure and establish important precedent for how future media consolidation attempts will be evaluated.

Beyond the regulatory questions, the merger has drawn criticism from press freedom advocates. When the Freedom of the Press Foundation attempted to air a critical advertisement about the deal on Paramount's streaming service, the company rejected it as a "conflict of interest." The 30-second spot criticized the network's leadership and raised concerns about press freedom implications of the merger.

Seth Stern, chief of advocacy for the Freedom of the Press Foundation, characterized Paramount's refusal as censorship. "Ellison won't air criticism of himself, his company, or his buddy Trump," Stern said, referencing Paramount's owner. The foundation subsequently posted the advertisement on its own website opposing the merger instead.

The lawsuit filed by the state coalition represents a significant legal obstacle to what would become one of the largest consolidations in entertainment industry history.

cards.headline: Ellen Burstyn to Receive Lifetime Achievement Award at Venice Film Festival
cards.teaser: The actress will be honored with the Golden Lion at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival.
cards.body:
Ellen Burstyn will receive the Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival, the festival announced. Her career includes notable performances in The Last Picture Show, The Exorcist, and Alice Doesn't Live Here Anymore.

Festival artistic director Alberto Barbera described Burstyn as an actress of rare intensity and truth. The Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement recognizes outstanding contributions to cinema over the course of a career.

cards.headline: Tyler Perry Responds to Sexual Assault Allegations
cards.teaser: The filmmaker claims his male accuser proposed a multimillion-dollar settlement before filing allegations.
cards.body:
Tyler Perry has stated that a man accusing him of sexual assault proposed a multimillion-dollar settlement prior to making public allegations. The filmmaker is now facing what his legal team describes as efforts to coerce a settlement through deposition motions.

The accuser's attorney has indicated that additional men may come forward with allegations against Perry. The filmmaker's legal response suggests he views the claims as part of a financial strategy rather than legitimate accusations.

cards.headline: National Youth Theatre Announces Stars for 70th Anniversary Performance
cards.teaser: Jack Thorne, India Amarteifio, and Judi Dench will participate in the September celebration in London.
cards.body:
The National Youth Theatre has revealed the first performers for Letters to My Younger Future Self, a one-night show celebrating the organization's 70th anniversary. The performance takes place on September 20 at London's Royal Festival Hall at Southbank Centre, with support from Netflix.

The lineup features BAFTA winner Jack Thorne, who co-created the series Adolescence, Bridgerton star India Amarteifio, and acclaimed actress Judi Dench. The show marks seven decades of the youth theater's dedication to developing young performers.

cards.headline: Webtoon Productions Partners with Espotlight for Spanish-Language Adaptations
cards.teaser: The companies will develop film and TV projects from Wattpad webnovels under a new first-look deal.
cards.body:
Webtoon Productions and Espotlight have signed a first-look agreement to develop Spanish-language film and television adaptations of Wattpad webnovels. The partnership expands on previous collaboration that produced Boulevard with Sony Pictures International.

Under the arrangement, Espotlight will have first access to Spanish-language stories published on Wattpad. The Madrid and Los Angeles-based company will evaluate webnovels for potential adaptation into visual media for Spanish-speaking audiences.

cards.headline: Stranger Things Actress Linnea Berthelsen to Debut on London Stage
cards.teaser: The performer will appear in Darkling at the Bush Theatre in her first UK stage role.
cards.body:
Linnea Berthelsen, known for playing Kali Prasad in the second and final season of Netflix's Stranger Things, will make her UK stage debut in Darkling at London's Bush Theatre. The solo play is presented by Actors Touring Company and co-produced with the Bush Theatre.

Berthelsen portrayed the character also known as 008 in the series. The production is described as an epic story, though the specific narrative and performance dates have not been detailed in the announcement.

cards.headline: Icelandic Producer Teams with ZDF Studios on Crime Drama Series
cards.teaser: Glassriver and Network Movie will adapt Lilja Sigurardóttir's bestselling Orra Investigation novels.
cards.body:
Icelandic producer Glassriver is partnering with ZDF Studios-owned Network Movie to develop Orra, a crime drama series based on Lilja Sigurardóttir's internationally bestselling novels. Network Movie has optioned all five books in the series.

The novels include Cold as Hell, Red as Blood, White as Snow, Dark as Night, and Deep as Death. The adaptation will bring the Icelandic crime stories to television audiences through the collaboration between the Icelandic and German production companies.

hero.headline: House GOP seeks end to floor standoff with conservative faction
hero.body:
House Republican leaders are working to resolve a weeks-long standoff with conservative members that has brought legislative activity to a halt. The dispute centers on demands from hard-line Republicans that party leaders take stronger action on the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act, known as the SAVE America bill.

The floor paralysis has prevented the House from conducting regular business for two weeks. Conservative members have used procedural tactics to block votes and other chamber activities until their demands are met. House GOP leaders are hoping to make progress on resolving the impasse, though the path forward remains uncertain.

The SAVE America Act relates to voter eligibility requirements, though conservative members have pressed for more aggressive moves on the legislation than leadership has been willing to pursue. The standoff represents a familiar challenge for House Speaker Mike Johnson, who like his predecessors has faced pressure from the party's most conservative wing to take harder-line positions on policy priorities.

The disruption comes as House Republicans hold a narrow majority, giving small groups of members significant leverage to influence the legislative agenda. Similar standoffs have occurred repeatedly in recent years, with conservative factions using procedural tools to extract concessions from leadership. The current impasse has prevented consideration of other legislation and routine chamber business.

Leadership hopes to see movement toward a resolution that would allow the House to resume normal operations. The duration of previous standoffs has varied, with some resolved within days and others stretching longer as negotiations continue between leadership and the demanding members.

cards.headline: Senate GOP agenda faces delays after Graham death, McConnell absence
cards.teaser: The death of Senate Budget Committee Chair Lindsey Graham and the absence of other key Republicans have disrupted the Senate majority leader's legislative plans.
cards.body:
The death of Sen. Lindsey Graham has significantly complicated the Republican legislative agenda as lawmakers return to Capitol Hill. Graham, who chaired the Senate Budget Committee and held senior positions on the Appropriations and Judiciary Committees, played a key role in negotiating party-line bills on defense spending and other presidential priorities.

Senate Republicans now face mounting obstacles beyond Graham's loss, including demands from Trump for new voting restrictions and the ongoing absence of Mitch McConnell. These disruptions arrive as both parties prepare for the November midterm elections, with control of Congress at stake. South Carolina's governor has selected Graham's sister to serve out the remainder of his term.

cards.headline: Congress considers quick passage of Russia sanctions bill as Graham tribute
cards.teaser: Lawmakers are pushing to advance bipartisan Russia sanctions legislation authored by the late Sen. Lindsey Graham as a way to honor him.
cards.body:
Supporters of Ukraine in Congress are urging swift passage of bipartisan Russia sanctions legislation that Graham had authored. Graham announced a breakthrough on the bill shortly before his death, saying lawmakers had reached agreement with the White House on the measure.

The push to move the legislation quickly represents an effort by colleagues to honor Graham's work on the issue. The bill addresses sanctions related to Russia, though the specific provisions were not detailed. Graham's announcement of the deal came late last week before his death on Saturday night.

cards.headline: South Carolina governor appoints Graham's sister to finish Senate term
cards.teaser: Gov. Henry McMaster has named Darline Graham to serve out the remainder of her brother's Senate term following his death.
cards.body:
South Carolina Governor Henry McMaster appointed Darline Graham Nordone to fill the Senate seat left vacant by her brother Lindsey Graham's death on Saturday. The appointment came after Donald Trump recommended her for the role.

Lawmakers from both parties welcomed Nordone's selection, viewing her as an appropriate successor to the senator who had raised her after their parents died during her teenage years. She will serve the remainder of Graham's current term.

cards.headline: Trump extends National Guard deployment in Washington through 2029
cards.teaser: The National Guard deployment to Washington ordered by President Trump has been extended multiple times and now runs until Inauguration Day 2029.
cards.body:
President Trump has extended the National Guard deployment in Washington, D.C. through Inauguration Day 2029. The deployment, which was initially ordered by presidential directive, has undergone several extensions since its inception.

The National Guard will maintain a continued presence in the nation's capital throughout the remainder of Trump's current term.

cards.headline: New York imposes statewide freeze on hyperscale data centers
cards.teaser: Gov. Kathy Hochul is pausing environmental permits for new hyperscale data centers for up to a year, the first such statewide action in the nation.
cards.body:
New York Gov. Kathy Hochul has signed the nation's first statewide moratorium on new hyperscale data centers. The freeze pauses state-level environmental permits for up to one year while the state develops regulatory guidelines.

The moratorium aims to protect the environment, the energy grid, and residents' electric bills amid growing concerns about the energy demands of large data facilities. A separate bill passed by the state legislature that could restrict even more data center developments is awaiting the governor's signature.

cards.headline: Google AI chief proposes US-led global watchdog for advanced models
cards.teaser: Demis Hassabis is calling for the US to establish an international AI regulator with authority to screen advanced models and coordinate industrywide slowdowns.
cards.body:
Demis Hassabis, co-founder and CEO of Google DeepMind, is calling for the establishment of a US-led global AI watchdog. The regulatory body would evaluate the world's most advanced AI models and coordinate an industry-wide slowdown if risks escalate.

Hassabis, a Nobel laureate overseeing development of Google's Gemini AI, told Axios that systematic international oversight of AI development is now necessary. He proposes funding the watchdog through technology industry contributions, outlined in his manifesto "A Framework for Frontier AI and the Dawning of a New Age."
